```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  cache = FALSE,
  comment = "#>",
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE
)
```

Fisheries catch composition data are often collected from non-representative
sampling programmes — observers may cover only a subset of the fleet, certain
areas or seasons may be over- or under-sampled, and spatial coverage can shift
over time. Naively treating these samples as representative of the whole fishery
can produce biased estimates of catch-at-age or catch-at-length compositions.

This vignette demonstrates how `ComPoM` can correct for such biases by:
fitting a Poisson-multinomial model with spatially varying coefficients
(via `sdmTMB`), then scaling the model predictions to known total catches
across the full fished area.

The simulation sets up a known truth — spatially varying selectivity, temporal
trends, and seasonal effects — then samples it with strong spatial and seasonal
bias. We compare a spatial model that accounts for the full domain against a
non-spatial model that cannot, showing that the spatial model recovers the true
compositions more accurately.

```{r setup}
library(tidyverse)
library(ComPoM)
library(sdmTMB)

source("vignette_helpers.R")

# Helper functions
clo <- function(x) x / sum(x)

# Simulation parameters
n_bins <- 10
n_samps <- 50
n_locations <- 250
n_seasons <- 4
n_per_samps <- 100
n_years <- 10

M <- 0.2

surv <- exp(-(1:n_bins) * M)
popfreq <- clo(surv)

# Selectivity parameters
L50_base <- 6.5
L95 <- 0.75
```

## Simulate Spatial Domain

Create a spatial grid with coordinates and simulate spatially-varying selectivity.

Figure 1 shows the simulated spatial effect on L50.

```{r simulate-spatial-domain, fig.width=7, fig.height=6}
#| fig.cap: >
#|   Figure 1. Simulated spatial effect on the selectivity parameter L50 (log scale) at the candidate
#|   locations.
set.seed(123)

# Create spatial locations (e.g., fishing locations)
locations <- data.frame(
  loc_id = 1:n_locations,
  x = runif(n_locations, 0, 100),
  y = runif(n_locations, 0, 100)
)

# Simulate spatial random field for selectivity variation
# Using a simple distance-based correlation structure
spatial_field <- function(x, y, range = 30, sigma = 0.3) {
  n <- length(x)
  dist_mat <- as.matrix(dist(cbind(x, y)))
  cov_mat <- sigma^2 * exp(-dist_mat / range)
  MASS::mvrnorm(1, rep(0, n), cov_mat)
}

# Generate spatial effect on L50
locations$spatial_effect <- spatial_field(locations$x, locations$y, range = 10, sigma = 0.5)

# Visualize spatial field
ggplot(locations, aes(x = x, y = y, color = spatial_effect)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  scale_color_viridis_c(option = "cividis", name = "Spatial\neffect") +
  coord_equal()
```

## Simulate Temporal and Seasonal Effects

```{r simulate-temporal-effects}
# Year effects (random walk)
year_effects <- cumsum(rnorm(n_years, 0, 0.1))

# Season effects
season_effects <- rnorm(n_seasons, 0, 0.2)
season_effects <- season_effects - mean(season_effects)

temporal_df <- expand_grid(
  Year = factor(1:n_years),
  Season = factor(1:n_seasons)
) |>
  mutate(
    year_effect = year_effects[as.integer(Year)],
    season_effect = season_effects[as.integer(Season)]
  )
```

## Generate True Catch Compositions

```{r true-catch-compositions}
# Full factorial of all strata with spatial coordinates
true_catch_by_bin <- expand_grid(
  loc_id = 1:n_locations,
  Year = factor(1:n_years),
  Season = factor(1:n_seasons),
  bin = 1:n_bins
) |>
  left_join(locations, by = "loc_id") |>
  left_join(temporal_df, by = c("Year", "Season")) |>
  mutate(
    L50 = exp(log(L50_base) + spatial_effect + year_effect + season_effect),
    catch = rgamma(n(), 100, 0.01),
    tcatch = Selectivity(bin, L50, L95) * popfreq[bin] * catch
  )

# Summarize true catch
true_catch_summary <- true_catch_by_bin |>
  group_by(Year, bin) |>
  summarise(tcatch = sum(tcatch), .groups = "drop")
```

## Simulate Non-Representative Sampling

Figure 2 shows the candidate and sampled locations.

```{r simulate-sampling, fig.width=7, fig.height=6}
#| fig.cap: >
#|   Figure 2. Candidate locations (grey) and locations that were sampled (orange).
# Sample locations with strong spatial bias (prefer high x AND high y corner)
sample_locations <- function(n_samps, locations) {
  # Strong bias towards the northeast corner of the domain
  probs <- exp(locations$x / 25 + locations$y / 25)
  probs <- probs / sum(probs)
  sample(locations$loc_id, n_samps, replace = TRUE, prob = probs)
}

# Season sampling probabilities that shift across years
# Early years oversample season 1, late years oversample season 4
season_probs_by_year <- function(year, n_years, n_seasons) {
  # Linear shift: weight moves from season 1 to season 4 over time
  alpha <- (year - 1) / (n_years - 1)  # 0 for year 1, 1 for last year
  weights <- numeric(n_seasons)
  weights[1] <- 4 * (1 - alpha) + 0.5 * alpha

  weights[n_seasons] <- 0.5 * (1 - alpha) + 4 * alpha
  # Middle seasons stay low
  if (n_seasons > 2) {
    weights[2:(n_seasons - 1)] <- 0.5
  }
  weights / sum(weights)
}

# Generate samples - distribute across years
set.seed(456)
samples <- tibble(
  samp_id = 1:(n_samps * n_years),
  Year = factor(rep(1:n_years, each = n_samps))
) |>
  mutate(
    loc_id = sample_locations(n(), locations),
    Season = factor(sapply(as.integer(Year), function(yr) {
      sample(1:n_seasons, 1, prob = season_probs_by_year(yr, n_years, n_seasons))
    }))
  ) |>
  left_join(locations, by = "loc_id") |>
  left_join(temporal_df, by = c("Year", "Season")) |>
  mutate(
    L50 = exp(log(L50_base) + spatial_effect + year_effect + season_effect)
  )

# Generate composition samples from each sampling event
long_form_sims <- samples |>
  group_by(samp_id) |>
  nest() |>
  mutate(
    comp_samps = lapply(data, function(df) {
      which(rmultinom(n_per_samps, 1,
                      Selectivity(1:n_bins, df$L50, L95) * popfreq) == 1,
            arr.ind = TRUE)[, 1]
    })
  ) |>
  unnest(c(data, comp_samps)) |>
  mutate(count = 1) |>
  rename(bin = comp_samps)

# Visualize sampling locations
ggplot() +
  geom_point(data = locations, aes(x = x, y = y, colour = "Candidate"), size = 2) +
  geom_point(data = long_form_sims |> distinct(loc_id, x, y),
             aes(x = x, y = y, colour = "Sampled"), alpha = 0.7, size = 2) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(Candidate = "grey70", Sampled = "orange"), name = NULL) +
  coord_equal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## Prepare Data and Create Mesh

```{r prepare-data-mesh, fig.width=5, fig.height=4}
# Prepare input data for ComPoM
input_data <- data_prep(
  long_form_sims,
  vars_for_grouping = c('loc_id', 'Year', 'Season', 'x', 'y'),
  bin_lab = 'bin'
) |>
  mutate(
    x = as.numeric(as.character(x)),
    y = as.numeric(as.character(y))
  )

# Create mesh for sdmTMB — use ALL fishing locations for the domain,
# not just the biased sample, so the mesh covers the full fished area
all_locs_sf <- sf::st_as_sf(locations, coords = c("x", "y"))
bnd <- fmesher::fm_nonconvex_hull(all_locs_sf, convex = -0.1, format = 'sf')
msh <- fmesher::fm_mesh_2d(locations[, c("x", "y")], cutoff = 3, boundary = bnd)
mesh <- make_mesh(input_data, xy_cols = c("x", "y"), mesh = msh)

bnd_vect <- terra::vect(bnd)
pg <- terra::rast(bnd_vect)
pg$lyr.1 <- 1

```

Figure 3 shows the mesh used for the spatial fields.

```{r mesh-figure, fig.width=5, fig.height=4.5}
#| fig.cap: >
#|   Figure 3. SPDE mesh (grey triangles), domain boundary (skyblue) and sampled locations (points).
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = fmesher::fm_as_sfc(msh), fill = NA, colour = "grey70", linewidth = 0.15) +
  geom_sf(data = bnd, fill = NA, colour = "skyblue", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(data = distinct(input_data, x, y), aes(x = x, y = y), size = 0.7) +
  labs(x = "x", y = "y")
```

## Fit Spatiotemporal Model with sdmTMB

```{r fit-spatiotemporal-model}
# Fit model with bin-specific spatially varying coefficients
mods_spatial <- fit_model(
  re_form = 'Season',
  ffx_form = 'Year',
  data = input_data,
  backend = 'TMB',
  mesh = mesh,
  time = "Year",
  coords = c("x", "y"),
  iter = 1000,
  warmup = 500,
  thin = 2
)

summary(mods_spatial$model)
```

## Fit Non-Spatial Model for Comparison

```{r fit-nonspatial-model}
mods_nonspatial <- fit_model(
  re_form = 'Season',
  ffx_form = 'Year',
  data = input_data,
  backend = 'TMB',
  iter = 1000,
  warmup = 500,
  thin = 2
)

summary(mods_nonspatial$model)
```

## Compare Model Fits

```{r compare-aic}
AIC(mods_spatial$model)
AIC(mods_nonspatial$model)
```

## Effects Plots

Figure 4 shows the year and season effects from the non-spatial and spatial models.

```{r effects-plots, fig.dim=c(14, 12)}
#| fig.cap: >
#|   Figure 4. Year effects (a, b) and season effects (c, d) on the composition, as multipliers relative to
#|   the geometric mean across bins, from the non-spatial model (a, c) and the spatial model
#|   (b, d). Points are medians and bars 95% intervals.
(Fx_plot(mods_nonspatial, grp = 'Year', grid = NULL) |
   Fx_plot(mods_spatial, grp = 'Year', grid = NULL)) /
  (Fx_plot(mods_nonspatial, grp = 'Season', grid = NULL) |
     Fx_plot(mods_spatial, grp = 'Season', grid = NULL)) +
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = "a")
```

## Scale Compositions to Catch

```{r scale-compositions, fig.dim=c(12,7)}
# Prepare scaling data for spatial model
IDs <- terra::extract(pg, true_catch_by_bin[, c('x', 'y')], ID = TRUE, xy = TRUE)
true_catch_by_bin[, colnames(IDs)] <- IDs

scale_df_spatial <- true_catch_by_bin |>
  group_by(Season, Year, x, y) |>
  summarise(catch = sum(tcatch), .groups = "drop")

# Prepare scaling data for non-spatial model
scale_df_nonspatial <- true_catch_by_bin |>
  semi_join(
    input_data |> ungroup() |> distinct(Year, Season),
    by = c("Year", "Season")
  ) |>
  group_by(Year, Season) |>
  summarise(catch = sum(tcatch), .groups = "drop")

# Scale compositions
scaled_comp_spatial <- scale_comps(
  scale_df_spatial,
  predvar = 'catch',
  fit = mods_spatial,
  grps = c('Season', 'Year')
)

scaled_comp_nonspatial <- scale_comps(
  scale_df_nonspatial,
  predvar = 'catch',
  fit = mods_nonspatial,
  grps = c('Year', 'Season')
)
```

## Compare Scaled Compositions to Truth

Figure 5 shows the scaled annual compositions of both models against the true composition.

```{r compare-compositions, fig.dim=c(12, 12)}
#| fig.cap: >
#|   Figure 5. Annual compositions of the catch from the spatial model (a) and the non-spatial model (b).
#|   Black points and bars are medians and 95% intervals, and skyblue points the true composition.
# True compositions by year
true_comp_year <- true_catch_by_bin |>
  group_by(Year, bin) |>
  summarise(tcatch = sum(tcatch), .groups = "drop")

# Spatial model (aggregate across seasons)
scaled_comp_spatial_yr <- scaled_comp_spatial |>
  group_by(Year, bin, .draw) |>
  summarise(tot_by_bin = sum(tot_by_bin), .groups = "drop")

p_truth_spatial <- scaled_comp_plot(
  scaled_comp = scaled_comp_spatial_yr,
  grps = 'Year',
  scaled = TRUE,
  scales = "free_y",
  comp_are = true_comp_year,
  cvar = 'tcatch',
  comp_label = "True"
)

# Non-spatial model (aggregate across seasons)
scaled_comp_nonspatial_yr <- scaled_comp_nonspatial |>
  group_by(Year, bin, .draw) |>
  summarise(tot_by_bin = sum(tot_by_bin), .groups = "drop")

p_truth_nonspatial <- scaled_comp_plot(
  scaled_comp = scaled_comp_nonspatial_yr,
  grps = 'Year',
  scaled = TRUE,
  scales = "free_y",
  comp_are = true_comp_year,
  cvar = 'tcatch',
  comp_label = "True"
)

p_truth_spatial / p_truth_nonspatial + plot_annotation(tag_levels = "a")
```

## Evaluate Model Performance

Figure 6 shows both models compared with the true and raw sample compositions.

```{r evaluate-performance, fig.dim=c(12, 18)}
#| fig.cap: >
#|   Figure 6. Annual compositions from the spatial model (a), relative error of the spatial model and of
#|   the raw samples against the true composition (b), and annual compositions from the
#|   non-spatial model (c). The true composition is skyblue and the raw sample composition orange.
#|   Black points and bars are medians and 95% intervals.
# Raw (biased) samples
raw_comp <- input_data |>
  group_by(Year, bin) |>
  summarise(tcatch = sum(tot_by_bin), .groups = "drop")

p_eval_spatial <- scaled_comp_plot(
  scaled_comp = scaled_comp_spatial_yr,
  grps = 'Year',
  scaled = TRUE,
  scales = "free_y",
  comp_are = true_comp_year,
  comp_are2 = raw_comp,
  cvar = 'tcatch',
  comp_label = "True",
  comp2_label = "Raw samples"
)

p_eval_error <- scaled_comp_comp(
  scaled_comp = scaled_comp_spatial_yr,
  grps = 'Year',
  scaled = TRUE,
  comp_are = true_comp_year,
  comp_are2 = raw_comp,
  cvar = 'tcatch'
)

p_eval_nonspatial <- scaled_comp_plot(
  scaled_comp = scaled_comp_nonspatial_yr,
  grps = 'Year',
  scaled = TRUE,
  scales = "free_y",
  comp_are = true_comp_year,
  comp_are2 = raw_comp,
  cvar = 'tcatch',
  comp_label = "True",
  comp2_label = "Raw samples"
)

p_eval_spatial / p_eval_error / p_eval_nonspatial +
  plot_layout(heights = c(1, 0.3, 1)) + plot_annotation(tag_levels = "a")
```

## Model Diagnostics

```{r model-diagnostics}
tidy(mods_spatial$model, "ran_pars")
```

The spatial model can better account for the non-representative sampling by modeling the underlying spatial structure in the data.

## Scenario Comparison

The spatial model reduced the error of the annual compositions relative to the non-spatial model
in the simulation above, and a part of the error remained. This section compares the two models
in ten scenarios to separate the error that the spatial model removed from the error that it did
not. The scenario code is in `scenario_helpers.R` and `run_scenarios.R`, and the results are
stored in `scenario_results.csv`.

### Scenario Design

Each scenario used the simulation code above with one or more changes (Table 1). The changes were
in the sampling footprint (fixed in the north-east corner, moving from the north-east to the
south-west over the years, or uniform with no seasonal shift), the range of the simulated spatial
field, a west-to-east gradient in log(L50), the number of fish per sample, and the width of the
length bins. All scenarios had 250 locations, 10 years, four seasons and 50 samples per year.
Each scenario was simulated once with the same seeds. Absolute errors are therefore comparable
within a scenario, and between scenarios they also reflect the differing realised fields.

Each scenario was fitted with the non-spatial model (year as fixed effect, season as nuisance
random effect) and with a spatial model that had bin-specific spatial fields and no
spatio-temporal fields (`fit_model(spatiotemporal = FALSE)`), because the simulated field is
constant over time. Scenario A also included
the model with spatio-temporal fields from `fit_model()`. Compositions were scaled to the true
catch of all 250 locations by catch weighting, as above, with 100 simulation draws.

The error was the mean absolute error (MAE) of the annual proportions, averaged over years and
bins, relative to the true catch composition of the full fishery. The error was split into a
component that was constant across years (the mean error of each bin over years) and a
year-varying component (the remainder). A constant error shifts all years equally and does not
change trends. The year-varying component includes sampling variation. The two components do not
sum to the MAE, because each is a mean of absolute values.

```{r scenario-data, include = FALSE}
scen_env <- new.env()
sys.source("scenario_helpers.R", envir = scen_env)
res <- read.csv("scenario_results.csv")
design <- purrr::map_dfr(scen_env$scenario_specs, function(s) {
  tibble(
    Scenario = s$name, Description = s$label,
    Footprint = if (isTRUE(s$smp$loc_bias == 0)) "uniform" else s$smp$footprint,
    `Field range` = s$range, Gradient = s$trend,
    `Fish per sample` = if (is.null(s$smp$n_per)) 100 else s$smp$n_per,
    `Bin width` = if (is.null(s$bin_width)) 1 else s$bin_width
  )
})
wide <- res |>
  filter(method %in% c("raw", "nonspatial", "spatial_only")) |>
  select(scenario, n_bins, n_locs_sampled, field_year1, field_lastyear, field_domain,
         method, MAE, const, varying) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = method, values_from = c(MAE, const, varying)) |>
  mutate(red_MAE = 1 - MAE_spatial_only / MAE_nonspatial,
         red_const = 1 - const_spatial_only / const_nonspatial,
         red_var = 1 - varying_spatial_only / varying_nonspatial) |>
  arrange(match(scenario, design$Scenario))
get <- function(s, col) wide[[col]][wide$scenario == s]
f4 <- function(x) formatC(x, digits = 4, format = "f")
f3 <- function(x) formatC(x, digits = 3, format = "f")
pct <- function(x) paste0(round(100 * x), "%")
pct1 <- function(x) paste0(round(100 * x, 1), "%")
# largest difference between the mean field at the sampled locations and the domain mean
field_gap <- function(s) {
  max(abs(c(get(s, "field_year1"), get(s, "field_lastyear")) - get(s, "field_domain")))
}
ten <- wide$n_bins == 10
full_A <- res |> filter(scenario == "A", method == "full")
sp_A <- res |> filter(scenario == "A", method == "spatial_only")
st_sd <- tidy(mods_spatial$model, "ran_pars") |>
  filter(term == "sigma_Z") |>
  pull(estimate) |>
  nth(2)
```

```{r scenario-table-design, echo = FALSE}
design |>
  left_join(wide |> select(Scenario = scenario, n_locs_sampled, field_year1, field_lastyear,
                           field_domain), by = "Scenario") |>
  mutate(across(starts_with("field_"), ~ round(.x, 2))) |>
  rename(`Locations sampled` = n_locs_sampled, `Field, year 1` = field_year1,
         `Field, year 10` = field_lastyear, `Field, domain` = field_domain) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = paste(
    "Table 1. Scenario settings and realised sampling. The field columns give the mean simulated",
    "effect on log(L50) at the sampled locations in the first and last year and over all 250",
    "locations. The field range is the range of the exponential covariance, and the gradient is",
    "the plus or minus change in log(L50) across the domain."))
```

### Scenario Results

```{r scenario-table-results, echo = FALSE}
wide |>
  left_join(design |> select(Scenario, Description), by = c("scenario" = "Scenario")) |>
  transmute(Scenario = scenario, Description, Bins = n_bins, Raw = round(MAE_raw, 4),
            `Non-spatial` = round(MAE_nonspatial, 4), Spatial = round(MAE_spatial_only, 4),
            `Reduction` = pct(red_MAE)) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = paste(
    "Table 2. MAE of the annual proportions for the raw samples, the non-spatial model and the",
    "spatial-only model, and the reduction from the non-spatial to the spatial model.",
    "Scenario F had 6 bins instead of 10, so its MAE is not comparable with the other scenarios."))
```

The non-spatial model reproduced the raw sample compositions (Table 2). Its MAE differed from the
MAE of the raw samples by at most `r f4(max(abs(wide$MAE_raw - wide$MAE_nonspatial)))` in every
scenario, because the year-by-bin fixed effects estimated the annual composition of the samples.

The spatial model had a lower MAE than the non-spatial model in every scenario, by
`r pct(min(wide$red_MAE))` (scenario `r wide$scenario[which.min(wide$red_MAE)]`) to
`r pct(max(wide$red_MAE))` (scenario `r wide$scenario[which.max(wide$red_MAE)]`). The constant
component was lower by `r pct(min(wide$red_const))` to `r pct(max(wide$red_const))`
(Figure 7a), and the reduction was larger than that of the year-varying component in all
scenarios except `r paste(wide$scenario[wide$red_const <= wide$red_var], collapse = ", ")`. The
year-varying component was lower by `r pct1(min(wide$red_var))` to `r pct1(max(wide$red_var))`
(Figure 7b). It was
`r f4(min(wide$varying_nonspatial[ten]))` to `r f4(max(wide$varying_nonspatial[ten]))` for the
non-spatial model and `r f4(min(wide$varying_spatial_only[ten]))` to
`r f4(max(wide$varying_spatial_only[ten]))` for the spatial model in the scenarios with 10 bins.

Figure 7 shows the scenario comparison.

```{r scenario-figure, echo = FALSE, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 4.8}
#| fig.cap: >
#|   Figure 7. Constant-over-years error (a) and year-varying error (b) of the annual
#|   compositions for the non-spatial model (skyblue) and the spatial-only model (orange) in each
#|   scenario. Scenario F had 6 bins and is not comparable in magnitude with the others.
library(cowplot)
library(patchwork)
fig_data <- res |>
  filter(method %in% c("nonspatial", "spatial_only")) |>
  left_join(design |> select(Scenario, Description), by = c("scenario" = "Scenario")) |>
  mutate(method = factor(method, c("nonspatial", "spatial_only"), c("Non-spatial", "Spatial")),
         scen = factor(paste0(scenario, "  ", Description),
                       levels = rev(paste0(design$Scenario, "  ", design$Description))))
fig_panel <- function(col, xlab) {
  ggplot(fig_data, aes(x = .data[[col]], y = scen)) +
    geom_line(aes(group = scen), colour = "grey60", linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_point(aes(colour = method), size = 2.8) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c("Non-spatial" = "skyblue", "Spatial" = "orange"), name = NULL) +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, NA), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
    labs(x = xlab, y = NULL) +
    theme_compom(font_size = 11)
}
(fig_panel("const", "Constant-over-years error (MAE)") +
    (fig_panel("varying", "Year-varying error (MAE)") +
       theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), plot.margin = margin(5.5, 5.5, 5.5, 16)))) +
  plot_layout(guides = "collect") + plot_annotation(tag_levels = "a") &
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r weighting-check}
stratum <- true_catch_by_bin |>
  group_by(loc_id, Year, Season) |>
  mutate(p = tcatch / sum(tcatch), catch_total = sum(tcatch)) |>
  ungroup()
annual_prop <- function(weight) {
  stratum |>
    mutate(v = p * weight) |>
    group_by(Year, bin) |>
    summarise(v = sum(v), .groups = "drop") |>
    group_by(Year) |>
    mutate(v = v / sum(v)) |>
    ungroup()
}
weighting_mae <- mean(abs(annual_prop(stratum$catch_total)$v - annual_prop(1)$v))
size_cor <- stratum |>
  group_by(loc_id, Year, Season) |>
  summarise(mean_bin = sum(bin * p), catch_total = first(catch_total), .groups = "drop") |>
  summarise(r = cor(mean_bin, catch_total)) |>
  pull(r)
```

Uniform sampling (scenarios D and H3) left a constant error of
`r f4(get("D", "const_nonspatial"))` and `r f4(get("H3", "const_nonspatial"))` in the non-spatial
model. This was lower than with the footprint in A (`r f4(get("A", "const_nonspatial"))`) and H1
(`r f4(get("H1", "const_nonspatial"))`) and was not zero, so a part of the constant error did not
depend on the sampling footprint. A likely contributor was catch weighting. The annual
composition with equal weight for every stratum differs from the catch-weighted composition even
without sampling and without a model. In the simulated world of scenario A, the two compositions
differed by an MAE of `r f4(weighting_mae)` (chunk above), and the stratum catch was correlated
with the mean size of the stratum (correlation `r f3(size_cor)`), because a stratum with larger
fish had a lower selected abundance. This was computed for the world of scenario A only.

A sample average weights strata by the number of samples and not by catch. The non-spatial model
predicts one composition per year and season, so the correlation between catch and size across
the strata of a year and season is not represented. The spatial model predicted each stratum
separately and weighted the predictions by catch in `scale_comps()`. It lowered the constant
error in D to `r f4(get("D", "const_spatial_only"))` and in H3 to
`r f4(get("H3", "const_spatial_only"))`. The contribution of the weighting was not tested
separately in D and H3.

The moving footprint changed the mean simulated field at the sampled locations from
`r f3(get("H2", "field_year1"))` in the first year to `r f3(get("H2", "field_lastyear"))` in the
last year with the gradient (H2), against a domain mean of `r f3(get("H2", "field_domain"))`. The
fixed footprint with the gradient (H1) sampled a field of `r f3(get("H1", "field_year1"))` in the
first year and `r f3(get("H1", "field_lastyear"))` in the last year. The raw MAE was lower with
the moving footprint than with the fixed footprint, `r f4(get("B", "MAE_raw"))` against
`r f4(get("A", "MAE_raw"))` without the gradient (B and A) and `r f4(get("H2", "MAE_raw"))` against
`r f4(get("H1", "MAE_raw"))` with it (H2 and H1). The moving footprint sampled
`r get("B", "n_locs_sampled")` locations instead of `r get("A", "n_locs_sampled")`. The year-varying
component of the non-spatial model was lower with the moving footprint
(`r f4(get("B", "varying_nonspatial"))` in B against `r f4(get("A", "varying_nonspatial"))` in A,
and `r f4(get("H2", "varying_nonspatial"))` in H2 against `r f4(get("H1", "varying_nonspatial"))`
in H1). The reduction by the spatial model was `r pct(get("B", "red_MAE"))` in B against
`r pct(get("A", "red_MAE"))` in A, and `r pct(get("H2", "red_MAE"))` in H2 against
`r pct(get("H1", "red_MAE"))` in H1.

With 300 fish per sample (G), the MAE of the non-spatial model was
`r f4(get("G", "MAE_nonspatial"))` against `r f4(get("A", "MAE_nonspatial"))` with 100 fish (A),
and its constant component was `r f4(get("G", "const_nonspatial"))` against
`r f4(get("A", "const_nonspatial"))` in A. The MAE of the spatial model fell from
`r f4(get("A", "MAE_spatial_only"))` to `r f4(get("G", "MAE_spatial_only"))`, a reduction of
`r pct(get("G", "red_MAE"))` relative to the non-spatial model. With wider bins (F), the reduction
was `r pct(get("F", "red_MAE"))`, against `r pct(get("A", "red_MAE"))` in A.

In the scenarios with a field range of 30 (E and C), the non-spatial MAE was
`r f4(get("E", "MAE_nonspatial"))` and `r f4(get("C", "MAE_nonspatial"))`, with constant components
of `r f4(get("E", "const_nonspatial"))` and `r f4(get("C", "const_nonspatial"))`. The spatial model
reduced the MAE by `r pct(get("E", "red_MAE"))` and `r pct(get("C", "red_MAE"))`. The mean field
at the sampled locations differed from the domain mean by at most `r f3(field_gap("E"))` in E and
`r f3(field_gap("C"))` in C (Table 1), against `r f3(field_gap("A"))` in A.

In scenario A, the model with spatio-temporal fields and the spatial-only model had an MAE of
`r f4(full_A$MAE)` and `r f4(sp_A$MAE)` and a constant component of `r f4(full_A$const)` and
`r f4(sp_A$const)`. The estimated spatio-temporal standard deviation of the model fitted above
was `r formatC(st_sd, format = "e", digits = 1)`, and the simulated field was constant over time.

The Hessian of the spatial-only fit was positive definite in all scenarios. `sanity()` reported at
least one problem in `r sum(!res$sanity_ok[res$method == "spatial_only"])` of the
`r sum(res$method == "spatial_only")` spatial-only fits. The errors were not checked against fits
with additional optimisation steps. Each scenario was a single realisation, so the reductions
described these simulated worlds and not an expected value. Scenarios with different field ranges
also had different realised fields, and their errors differed for that reason in addition to the
change in the design.

## Oceanographic Influence on Compositions

Environmental covariates such as sea surface temperature (SST) can drive
spatial and temporal shifts in fish size compositions independently of the
year and season effects of primary interest. A recurring oceanographic cycle
such as El Niño shifts fish size availability. Warm SST occurs about every 5 years. In warm
years larger fish are more available, and in cold years smaller fish are.

Including SST as a smooth spline (`spl = "by_factor"`) separates the
oceanographic signal from the year fixed effects. `scale_comps()` can then
either retain the SST effect (compositions as observed under the ENSO cycle)
or remove it by evaluating the spline at mean SST (`sst_c = 0`), giving
year compositions standardised to average oceanographic conditions.

### Simulate ENSO-Like SST Cycle

We simulate a 5-year sinusoidal SST cycle (peaks at years 2, 7; troughs at
years 5, 10) plus independent spatial noise. The spatial noise is zero-centred
within each year so the within-year mean SST equals the cycle value — SST
carries both a temporal trend and within-year spatial variation.

```{r sst-simulate}
set.seed(42)

# 5-year sinusoidal ENSO cycle: warm years 2, 3, 7, 8 — cold years 4, 5, 9, 10
sst_cycle <- 1.5 * sin(2 * pi * (1:n_years - 1) / 5)
cat("SST cycle by year:", round(sst_cycle, 2), "\n")

# Spatial SST: temporal cycle + zero-centred spatial noise per year
sst_loc_year_enso <- purrr::map_dfr(1:n_years, function(yr) {
  spatial_noise <- spatial_field(locations$x, locations$y, range = 30, sigma = 0.4) +
                   rnorm(nrow(locations), 0, 0.1)
  locations |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      Year     = factor(yr),
      sst_spat = spatial_noise - mean(spatial_noise),
      sst_c    = sst_cycle[yr] + sst_spat
    )
})

# Verify within-year SST mean tracks the cycle
sst_loc_year_enso |>
  dplyr::group_by(Year) |>
  dplyr::summarise(mean_sst = round(mean(sst_c), 2),
                   sd_sst   = round(sd(sst_c),   2)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(cycle = round(sst_cycle, 2))
```

### Simulate SST-Shifted Compositions

Warm SST shifts L50 upward — larger fish become more available.

```{r sst-resample}
set.seed(42)

L50_sst_base <- 5
L95_sst      <- 8

input_sst_enso <- true_catch_by_bin |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    sst_loc_year_enso |> dplyr::select(loc_id, Year, sst_c),
    by = c("loc_id", "Year")
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    L50_use = L50_sst_base + 1.5 * sst_c,
    sel_use = Selectivity(bin, L50_use, L95_sst),
    avail   = popfreq[bin] * sel_use
  ) |>
  dplyr::group_by(loc_id, Year, Season) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    prob   = avail / sum(avail),
    counts = as.integer(rmultinom(1, n_per_samps, prob))
  ) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::select(loc_id, Year, Season, bin, counts, sst_c)

# Verify: proportion of large fish tracks the ENSO cycle
input_sst_enso |>
  dplyr::group_by(Year) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    prop_large = round(sum(counts[bin >= 6]) / sum(counts), 3),
    mean_sst   = round(mean(sst_c), 2)
  )
```

### Aggregate to SST Quintile Strata

SST quintiles are computed within each year, preserving both the temporal
cycle and within-year spatial variation independently of the year dummies.

```{r sst-aggregate}
input_sst_binned_enso <- input_sst_enso |>
  dplyr::group_by(Year) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    sst_q   = dplyr::ntile(sst_c, 5),
    sst_mid = tapply(sst_c, sst_q, mean)[as.character(sst_q)]
  ) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::group_by(Year, Season, sst_q, sst_mid, bin) |>
  dplyr::summarise(counts = sum(counts), .groups = "drop")

prep_sst_enso <- data_prep(
  comp              = input_sst_binned_enso |> dplyr::mutate(sst_c = sst_mid),
  vars_for_grouping = c("Year", "Season", "sst_q", "sst_c"),
  bin_lab           = "bin",
  count_var         = "counts"
)

cat("Unique SST values:", length(unique(prep_sst_enso$sst_c)), "\n")
```

### Fit Model with SST Smooth

`spl = "by_factor"` fits `s(sst_c, by=bin, k=4)` — a separate 1D smooth of
SST for each bin level, capturing bin-specific responses to SST (large bins
increase more in warm years). This is full-rank alongside `factor(Year):bin`
because SST varies across quintile strata within each year independently of
the year dummies. `Season` enters as nuisance RE via `re_form`.

```{r sst-fit}
mods_sst_enso <- suppressWarnings(fit_model(
  ffx_form = "Year",
  re_form  = "Season",
  cvars    = "sst_c",
  spl      = "by_factor",
  knots    = "4",
  data     = prep_sst_enso,
  backend  = "TMB",
  iter     = 1000,
  warmup   = 500,
  thin     = 2
))

mods_sst_enso$model <- sdmTMB::run_extra_optimization(
  mods_sst_enso$model, newton_loops = 2
)
sanity(mods_sst_enso$model)
```

### Year Effects After Accounting for SST

Figure 8 shows the year effects after accounting for the SST spline.

```{r sst-fx-plot, fig.dim=c(12, 5)}
#| fig.cap: >
#|   Figure 8. Year effects on the composition (multipliers) after accounting for the ENSO SST spline.
Fx_plot(mods_sst_enso, grp = "Year")
```

### Scale Compositions — Retaining vs Removing ENSO Signal

`mode = "catch"` evaluates all model terms at the
values of each stratum. The SST spline is evaluated at the observed quintile
midpoint and the Season random effect at the stratum's season. `Season` must
therefore be in `grps`.

`mode = "index"` sets the Season random effect (a selectivity term) to the population level,
and `sst_c = 0` in the grid evaluates the spline at mean SST. This gives year compositions
standardised to average oceanographic conditions and to the population level
of the season effect, removing the ENSO signal. In an application the weight
would be a predicted CPUE or abundance per stratum. Here the simulated catch
was used as the weight for both settings, so that only the treatment of the
model terms differed.

```{r sst-scale}
true_comp_sst_enso <- input_sst_binned_enso |>
  dplyr::group_by(Year, bin) |>
  dplyr::summarise(tcatch = sum(counts), .groups = "drop")

# Catch apportioned equally across 5 SST quintiles within each Year x Season
scale_df_sst_enso <- input_sst_binned_enso |>
  dplyr::distinct(Year, Season, sst_q, sst_c = sst_mid) |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    scale_df_nonspatial |> dplyr::select(Year, Season, catch),
    by = c("Year", "Season")
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(catch = catch / 5)

# ENSO signal retained (catch weighting: Season at each stratum's level)
scaled_enso_with <- suppressWarnings(scale_comps(
  scale_df        = scale_df_sst_enso,
  predvar         = "catch",
  fit             = mods_sst_enso,
  grps            = c("Year", "Season", "sst_q"),
  mode            = "catch"
))

# ENSO signal removed: SST set to 0 (mean), Season RE set to the population level (index mode)
scaled_enso_without <- suppressWarnings(scale_comps(
  fit      = mods_sst_enso,
  mode     = "index",
  grps     = c("Year", "Season", "sst_q"),
  grid     = scale_df_sst_enso |> dplyr::mutate(sst_c = 0),
  weight   = "catch"
))
```

### Compare Annual Compositions

Figure 9 shows the compositions with the SST effect retained and removed.

```{r sst-compare, fig.dim=c(12, 10)}
#| fig.cap: >
#|   Figure 9. Annual compositions with the SST effect retained, i.e. the observed ENSO cycle (a), and
#|   with the SST effect removed, i.e. standardised to mean SST = 0 (b). Skyblue points are
#|   the true composition.
enso_with_yr <- scaled_enso_with |>
  dplyr::group_by(Year, bin, .draw) |>
  dplyr::summarise(tot_by_bin = sum(tot_by_bin), .groups = "drop")

enso_without_yr <- scaled_enso_without |>
  dplyr::group_by(Year, bin, .draw) |>
  dplyr::summarise(tot_by_bin = sum(tot_by_bin), .groups = "drop")

p_enso_with <- scaled_comp_plot(
  scaled_comp = enso_with_yr, grps = "Year", scaled = TRUE,
  comp_are    = true_comp_sst_enso, cvar = "tcatch", comp_label = "True"
)

p_enso_without <- scaled_comp_plot(
  scaled_comp = enso_without_yr, grps = "Year", scaled = TRUE,
  comp_are    = true_comp_sst_enso, cvar = "tcatch", comp_label = "True"
)

p_enso_with / p_enso_without + plot_annotation(tag_levels = "a")
```

With SST retained (panel a), warm ENSO years (2, 7) show relatively more large
fish and cold years (4, 5, 9, 10) show small-fish-dominated compositions,
matching the simulated truth (skyblue points). With SST removed (panel b),
predictions converge toward the mean-SST composition — the ENSO-driven
inter-annual variability is standardised out, isolating the residual year
fixed effects from the oceanographic forcing.
